title: Pressure and Altitude Calculator
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Correct a station reading to sea level, see it in five units at once, and settle whether a difference between two stations is weather or geography.

learningObjectives: Solve for sea level pressure given a station reading and elevation.
Convert between all common pressure units.
Evaluate whether a pressure difference between two stations is weather or elevation.

keyQuestions: Why must every station report pressure corrected to sea level?
Your neighbour 300 m uphill reads 35 hPa lower. Is that a storm?
Why is flying from high pressure into low the dangerous direction?
commonMisconceptions: Comparing raw station pressures between places at different elevations.
Believing the correction is a small refinement.
Thinking hPa and mbar are different units rather than the same size.
assessmentOpportunities: Computes a sea level correction from an elevation without prompting.
Decomposes a two-station difference into elevation and weather.
Explains why an altimeter set to the wrong pressure is dangerous in one direction more than the other.
